properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch means water levels above flood stage are possible, but
not yet certain, based upon the latest forecasts. Persons along
rivers and streams in the watch area should monitor the latest
forecasts and be prepared to take action should flooding develop.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by late tonight.

properties.areaDesc: Benton County Lowlands; Linn County Lowlands; Lane County Lowlands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 7:29AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
Areas of dense fog in the southern Willamette Valley, including
lowland potions of Benton, Linn, and Lane Counties, may result in
hazardous travel conditions due to visibility of one half mile or
less.

If encountering fog, drivers should slow down, increase following
distance between vehicles, and remember to use low beams to
minimize glare. Pedestrians and cyclists should wear reflective
clothing and use lights to increase visibility to drivers.

Fog is expected to diminish in coverage by 10 AM PDT this morning.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 20 at 10:16AM AST until September 20 at 3:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Athens, OH; Gallia, OH; Meigs, OH; Washington, OH; Jackson, WV; Mason, WV; Wood, WV
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 20 at 10:09AM EDT until September 20 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall earlier this morning
continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Northeastern Gallia County in southeastern Ohio...
Meigs County in southeastern Ohio...
Southwestern Washington County in southeastern Ohio...
North Central Jackson County in northwestern West Virginia...
Southwestern Wood County in northwestern West Virginia...
North Central Mason County in western West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1008 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- The gauge on the Shade River has breached 16 feet, or minor flood
stage, and continues to rise. At that stage, the low spot on
Scout Camp Road near Sugar Run Creek bridge floods. Agricultural
fields adjacent to river begin to flood.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Parkersburg, Athens, Pomeroy, Coolville, Rutland, Forked Run
State Park, New Haven, Mason, Tuppers Plains, Washington, Lubeck,
Mineralwells, Middleport, Chester, Syracuse, Hartford City,
Darwin, Reedsville, Belleville, and Portland.
- This includes Interstate 77 in West Virginia near mile marker
151...and between mile markers 164 and 171.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 4:32AM MDT until September 20 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
Showers are turning light and tapering off along the western
foothills, but healthier showers will continue over central and
eastern portions of the forecast area today. The risk of flooding
continues.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible, along
with flash flooding over recent burn scars.

* WHERE...Southeast Montana and Sheridan County Wyoming.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in
poor drainage and urban areas. The risk of flooding will diminish
late this afternoon and evening as showers taper off.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The heaviest rainfall is slowly shifting eastward to southeast
Montana and northeast Wyoming.
- The Elk and McGhee-Remington burn scars are particularly
vulnerable to flash flooding and debris flows. Any other burn
scars from this summer will have elevated flash flood potential
as well.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 1:49AM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of low pressure systems will move through the panhandle
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the light rain will continue Saturday evening before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday night into Sunday
morning bringing moderate to heavy rain fall. Rain showers will
then take over on Sunday that may bring occasional moderate to
heavy rainfall as well.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 2:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy
showers and thunderstorms dropping south early in the week.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

NWSheadline: HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE THROUGH MIDWEEK... ...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Mississippi River at Ill. City LD16.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning to Thursday evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

The next statement will be issued by Sunday evening.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Chena River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 19 at 4:22AM AKDT until September 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows
remain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 412 AM AKDT, gage reports indicated widespread moderate to
heavy rain across the Chena River Basin over the past several
days. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain has fallen this week.

- High water levels will continue to work through the Fairbanks,
Badger, and North Pole region along the Chena and Little Chena
Rivers. Use extra caution on and along the rivers as water levels
continue to run at near record to record levels for this time of
year. The Chena River near Two Rivers is dropping but remains
bankfull. The Chena River below Hunts Creek is dropping but
remains bankfull. The Chena River below Moose Creek Dam is
cresting. The Chena River at Fairbanks will be cresting Saturday
afternoon. We are expecting rivers to remain high through the
weekend but gradually drop towards more normal levels through the
week.

- For Chena River below Hunts Creek near Two Rivers :
At 4:00am the stage was 15.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.2 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 15.3 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


For Chena River below Moose Creek dam:
At 4:00am the stage was 24.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 24.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 24.8 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


For Chena River near Two Rivers:
At 3:00am the stage was 19.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 19.1 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown, when encountering flooded roads.
